calls.reason: Studies from 2017 to 2022 show lasting weaknesses in reading comprehension, analogy and commonsense, but the PaLM results show large gains. Nothing measures broad reliability the same way over the five years, so 'scarcely changed' can't be called.
This is a hedged ('I don't think') necessity claim with no deadline. The MLTRL proposal existed before the post but doesn't settle whether it was 'good', and no verified AGI exists to test the claim.

CoCa's ImageNet score supports strong object recognition, and LLM planners had real limits. But PaLM's broad language results cut against the claim, and nothing compares the domains on a common scale.

The 2029 deadline hasn't passed. M2F's textbook-scale work and Anthropic's Fermat's Last Theorem formalization are major advances, but they are hand-picked projects, not shown conversion of arbitrary literature proofs.
The 2029 deadline is still ahead. YORI cooks only in a structured custom kitchen, and Figure's tests in unseen homes didn't include cooking, so the outcome isn't decided.

This is a general causal opinion. The only evidence, an overtrust study, measures trust built up over repeated successes, not whether people underestimate how hard AI problems are, so it can't be called.
